claims.text: A conformal WS2 coating deposited by PVD on high-entropy-alloy components will reduce coefficient of friction across a wide service-temperature range.
A conformal WS2 coating deposited by PVD on high-entropy-alloy components will reduce wear rate across a wide service-temperature range.
The WS2 coating forms a durable, low-shear-strength tribolayer during sliding.
The WS2 tribolayer minimizes direct asperity contact.
The proposed intervention is an adherent, continuous WS2 coating approximately 100–300 nm thick applied by physical vapor deposition.
The proposed service and testing range extends from ambient temperature to approximately 600°C in controlled service-relevant atmospheres.
Sliding transforms or maintains the WS2 coating as a self-lubricating, low-shear-strength tribofilm at the moving interface.
WS2 provides a chemically stable and lubricious interface over the proposed service-temperature range.
The WS2 interface limits metal-to-metal contact.
A sacrificial WS2 tribolayer prevents high local stresses and adhesive wear.
The coating is predicted to reduce coefficient of friction by approximately 30–50% relative to untreated high-entropy alloy under comparable conditions.
The coating is predicted to produce a marked decrease in wear rate relative to untreated high-entropy alloy across the temperature range.
Untreated high-entropy-alloy surfaces have relatively higher friction and accelerated wear because of direct asperity contact.
The benefit should persist only while WS2 retains its lubricious phase.
Above a likely WS2 stability limit of approximately 600°C, the coating may degrade and its tribological benefit may diminish.
Friction and wear reduction may vary with coating microstructure and deposition parameters.
Long-term coating adhesion, thermal-cycling resistance, and oxidation resistance on a heterogeneous high-entropy-alloy substrate are uncertain.

The hypothesis will be falsified if coated samples fail to achieve a statistically significant improvement, including at least a 30% friction reduction with a corresponding wear reduction across the tested range, or if premature coating degradation compromises functionality.
